paragraphs: We are a life sciences company focused on advancing a portfolio of current and future gene therapy candidates, which we refer to collectively as our Candidates, including SGT-003 for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy ("Duchenne"), SGT-212 for the treatment of Friedreich's ataxia ("FA"), SGT-501 for the treatment of Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia ("CPVT"), SGT-601 for the treatment of TNNT2-mediated dilated cardiomyopathy ("TNNT2 DCM"), and additional assets for the treatment of genetic cardiac and neuromuscular diseases, at different stages of development, with varying levels of investment. We are advancing our diverse pipeline across rare neuromuscular and cardiac diseases, bringing together experts in science, technology, disease management and care. Patient-focused and founded by those directly impacted by Duchenne, our mission is to improve the daily lives of patients living with these devastating diseases.

Solid was purpose-built to advance the best science and accelerate the discovery and development of treatments that may benefit all patients with Duchenne. As we expand to bring meaningful treatments to patients living with other neuromuscular and cardiac diseases, the values and guiding principles that drive us continue. Our corporate vision is to build an innovation platform enabling the discovery and development of high-value genetic medicines for neuromuscular and cardiac diseases by integrating internal capabilities, including a vector core, use of validated animal models, optimized expression cassettes, novel capsids and regulatory expertise, and collaborations with leaders in related clinical and research fields. Our mission, which guides our operations, is to treat and change the course of neuromuscular and cardiac diseases at all stages. Underscoring this mission, our disease-focused business model is founded on the following fundamental principles:
• identify and develop meaningful therapies for underserved patients with sometimes fatal neuromuscular and cardiac diseases;
• build innovative libraries of delivery capsids and other enabling technologies with the potential to have broad impact on the gene therapy field at large;
• bring together the leading experts in neuromuscular and cardiac diseases, science, technology, disease management and care; and
• be guided by the needs of these patients.

We are focused on developing transformative treatments to improve the lives of patients with rare neuromuscular and cardiac diseases. The majority of our current programs are designed to treat these diseases with gene transfer products. Gene transfer, a type of gene therapy, is designed to address diseases caused by mutated genes through the delivery of functional versions of genes, called transgenes. The transgenes are then utilized by the body to produce proteins that act therapeutically to treat the condition. In addition to a transgene, our gene transfer Candidates include a viral capsid or vector (a protein shell utilized as a vehicle to deliver a transgene to cells in the body) and a promoter (a specialized DNA sequence that directs cells to produce the protein in specific tissues). The capsid is modified to no longer self-replicate yet still retain its ability to introduce new genetic material directly into patients' cells. Adeno-associated virus ("AAV") capsids have been approved for use to deliver transgenes to patients, including via systemic delivery as well as stereotactic neurosurgical administration to the brain. The use of AAV capsids to deliver gene therapies has also been extensively studied by third parties in human clinical trials for multiple disease indications.
The following pipeline chart summarizes the development stages of our Candidates:

Duchenne is a genetic muscle-wasting disease predominantly affecting boys, with symptoms that usually manifest between three and five years of age. Duchenne is a progressive, irreversible, and ultimately fatal disease that affects approximately one in every 5,000 live male births and has an estimated prevalence of 10,000 to 15,000 cases in the United States alone, with at least 400 annual Duchenne births. Duchenne is caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene, which result in the absence or near-absence of dystrophin protein. Dystrophin protein works to strengthen muscle fibers and protect them from daily wear and tear. Dystrophin protein also serves as the cornerstone of the dystrophin glycoprotein complex ("DGC"), a group of proteins that links the inner and outer components of muscle cells to ensure proper muscle function. Without functioning dystrophin and DGC, muscles suffer excessive damage from normal daily activities and are unable to regenerate, leading to the build-up of fibrotic, or scar, and fat tissue. More than 1,000 dystrophin gene mutations, which can be inherited or can occur spontaneously, have been identified in people with Duchenne. By their early teens, Duchenne patients typically lose their ability to walk and become dependent on a wheelchair for mobility. By their 20s, patients essentially become paralyzed from the neck down and require a ventilator to breathe. Though disease severity and life expectancy vary, a patient's quality of life dramatically decreases over time, with death typically occurring by early adulthood from either cardiac or respiratory complications.

There is no cure for Duchenne. Glucocorticoid treatment, the current standard-of-care, has been shown to temporarily improve muscle strength, prolong the period of ambulation and slow the progression of Duchenne. However, glucocorticoid use is associated with well-known adverse side effects, including: severe weight gain, stunted growth, weakening of bone structure and metabolic dysfunctions, among others. The most commonly used glucocorticoids include prednisone and deflazacort (EMFLAZA).

Despite recent therapeutic advances, including the FDA approval of ELEVIDYS®, a gene transfer therapy for patients with Duchenne, we believe Duchenne represents a significant unmet medical need, in addition to a societal and economic burden. The economic burden includes costs associated with hospital admissions, medication, frequent doctor visits and investment in

assistive devices, as well as indirect costs related to productivity losses for the caregivers and costs due to pain, anxiety and social handicap. Only a small proportion of Duchenne patients are employed and many caregivers reduce their hours or stop working altogether to care for their children, who progressively require more help with everyday tasks, such as eating, dressing and using the bathroom. In some cases, patients also experience serious mental health issues that require additional support and treatment.

Our lead neuromuscular, investigational gene transfer candidate, SGT-003, is designed to address the underlying genetic cause of Duchenne by delivering a synthetic transgene that produces microdystrophin, a dystrophin-like protein that retains critical components of the full-size dystrophin gene, yet is small enough to fit within AAV packaging constraints, and is primarily expressed in muscles of the body, including skeletal, cardiac and respiratory muscles. AAV-SLB101, the capsid used in SGT-003, was generated by modifying a naturally occurring, non-pathogenic virus called AAV, with the goal of enhancing its ability to efficiently enter skeletal, diaphragm and cardiac muscle tissues. In March 2026, we began using the mark POLARIS-101TM to represent our AAV-SLB101 capsid product ("POLARIS-101TM").

Our microdystrophin is based on three decades of development and optimization work at the University of Missouri and the University of Washington as well as other academic institutions. In preclinical studies, the laboratories of Jeffrey Chamberlain, Ph.D., from the University of Washington, and Dongsheng Duan, Ph.D., from the University of Missouri, identified a proprietary configuration of genetic components that, when administered systemically, produces functional microdystrophin protein expression that not only stabilizes muscle membranes and protects muscle against injury, but also simultaneously restores the localization of DGC to the muscle membrane, notably increasing neuronal Nitric Oxide Synthase, ("nNOS") concentration. In published studies, Dr. Duan and Dr. Chamberlain demonstrated in animal models that, in comparison to earlier configurations, nNOS-restoring microdystrophins were more effective in improving muscle function and resistance to fatigue.

headings: Risks Related to our Financial Position and Need for Capital Requirements
We have incurred significant net losses since inception and anticipate that we will continue to incur net losses for the foreseeable future and may never achieve or maintain profitability.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our existing stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or Candidates.
We have never generated revenue from product sales and do not expect to do so for the foreseeable future, if ever.
Our limited operating history may make it difficult for our stockholders to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability.
Unfavorable global economic conditions could harm our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Risks Related to the Development of our Candidates

One of our prior clinical trials had been placed on clinical hold by the FDA in the past, and we cannot guarantee that similar events will not happen in ongoing, planned and future clinical trials for our Candidates.
We have never completed a clinical trial and may be unable to do so for any Candidate, including SGT-003, SGT-212, SGT-501 and other Candidates.
Success in preclinical studies or early clinical trials may not be indicative of results obtained in later trials.
We may encounter substantial delays in our clinical trials or we may fail to demonstrate safety and efficacy to the satisfaction of applicable regulatory authorities.
If our third-party clinical trial vendors fail to comply with strict regulations, any clinical trials for our Candidates may be delayed or unsuccessful.
We may find it difficult to enroll participants in our clinical trials, which could delay or prevent us from proceeding with clinical trials of SGT-003, SGT-212, SGT-501 or our other Candidates.

Even if we complete the necessary clinical trials, we cannot predict when, or if, we will obtain regulatory approval to commercialize our Candidates and the approval may be for a narrower indication than we seek.
Even if we obtain regulatory approval for a Candidate, our Candidates will remain subject to regulatory oversight.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors, in addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the section of this report titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our financial statements and related notes. If any of the events described in the following risk factors and the risks described elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K occurs, our business, operating results and financial condition could be seriously harmed and the trading price of our common stock could decline. This Annual Report on Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of factors that are described below and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks not presently known to us or other factors not perceived by us to present significant risks to our business at this time also may impair our business operations.

Since inception, we have incurred significant net losses. Our net losses were $174.3 million and $124.7 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $957.8 million. Prior to our acquisition of AavantiBio, Inc. in December 2022 (the "Acquisition") we devoted substantially all of our efforts to research and development, including clinical development of SGT-001, which we are no longer developing, and preclinical development of SGT-003, as well as to building out our management team and infrastructure. Following the Acquisition, we have devoted our efforts to the research and development of our other Candidates, including clinical development of SGT‑003, SGT‑212 and SGT-501, as well as building out our management team. We expect that it could be several years before we have a commercialized product, and we may never have a commercialized product. We expect to incur significant expenses and operating losses for the foreseeable future. We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if, and as, we:
• enroll participants in our INSPIRE DUCHENNE, IMPACT DUCHENNE, FALCON and ARTEMIS trials and advance clinical development of SGT-003, SGT-212 and SGT-501;
• advance our other Candidates into clinical trials;
• continue research and preclinical development of our Candidates and adjacent technologies such as assays;
• seek to identify additional Candidates; • engage in regulatory interactions with the FDA and other regulatory authorities;

During the year ended December 31, 2025, operating activities used $156.3 million of cash, primarily resulting from our net loss of $174.3 million offset by non-cash charges of $24.9 million due primarily to equity-based compensation of $16.9 million, an increase in the fair value of the derivative liabilities of $6.1 million, non-cash lease expense of $2.4 million, and depreciation expense of $1.6 million, partially offset by amortization of discount on available-for sale-securities of $1.9 million. During the year ended December 31, 2024, operating activities used $100.0 million of cash, primarily resulting from our net loss of $124.7 million offset by non-cash charges of $21.8 million due primarily to equity-based compensation of $10.5 million, an increase in the fair value of the derivative liabilities of $4.8 million, non-cash acquired in-process research and development of $3.4 million, depreciation expense of $2.5 million, non-cash lease expense of $2.4 million, and a non-cash upfront equity payment for a collaboration and license agreement of $2.0 million, partially offset by amortization of discount on available-for sale-securities of $3.6 million. paragraphs: 本公司為一生命科學公司，專注於推進現有及未來基因治療候選藥物組合，我們 collectively 稱為 Candidates，包括 SGT-003 用於治療杜氏肌肉營養不良症（"杜氏"），SGT-212 用於治療佛瑞德里希共濟失調症（"FA"），SGT-501 用於治療兒茶酚胺性多形性心室心動過速症（"CPVT"），SGT-601 用於治療 TNNT2 所致擴張型心肌病（"TNNT2 DCM"），以及用於治療遺傳性心臟及神經肌肉疾病的其他資產，這些資產處於不同開發階段，並具有不同層次的投資。本公司正在推進多樣化的開發管道，針對罕見的神經肌肉及心臟疾病，結合科學、科技、疾病管理及照護方面的專家。以患者為中心，並由直接受杜氏影響的人士所創立，我們的使命是改善患有這些致命疾病的患者的日常生活。

Solid 是專為推進最佳科學並加速發現及開發可能對所有杜氏患者有益的治療方案而設立的。隨著我們擴展，為患有其他神經肌肉及心臟疾病的患者帶來有意義的治療方案，驅動我們的價值觀與指導原則持續不變。我們的企業願景是建立一個創新平台，透過整合內部能力，包括載體核心、使用經過驗證的動物模型、優化表達 cassette、新型 capsid 及監管專業知識，並與相關臨牀及研究領域的領導者合作，發現及開發高價值的遺傳藥物，用於神經肌肉及心臟疾病。我們的使命，指導我們的運作，是治療並改變神經肌肉及心臟疾病在各階段的病程。強調此使命，我們的以疾病為中心的商業模式建立在以下基本原則上：
• 識別並開發對罕見且有時致命的神經肌肉及心臟疾病患者有意義的治療方案；
• 建立創新庫存的遞送 capsids 及其他啟動技術，這些技術有潛力對整個基因治療領域產生廣泛影響；
• 組合神經肌肉及心臟疾病、科學、科技、疾病管理及照護方面的領先專家；以及
• 以這些患者的需要為導向。

本公司專注於開發具有變革性的治療方案，以改善患有罕見神經肌肉及心臟疾病的患者的日常生活。目前我們的大多數計畫都是設計用來透過基因轉移產品治療這些疾病。基因轉移是一種基因治療，旨在透過交付功能性基因（稱為 transgene）來解決由突變基因引起的疾病。這些 transgene 會被身體用來產生具有治療作用的蛋白質以治療該疾病。除了 transgene 之外，我們的基因轉移 Candidates 還包括一種病毒 capsid 或 vector（一種用作將 transgene 傳遞至體內細胞的蛋白質殼）及一個 promoter（一種特殊的 DNA 序列，指導細胞在特定組織中產生蛋白質）。該 capsid 已經修改，使其不再自我複製，但仍保留將新遺傳物質直接引入患者細胞的能力。腺相關病毒（"AAV"）capsid 已經獲准用於將 transgene 傳遞至患者，包括透過全身性給藥以及立體定向神經外科手術給藥至腦部。第三方也已廣泛研究使用 AAV capsid 來遞送基因治療藥物在多種疾病指徵的人類臨牀試驗中。
以下為我們 Candidates 的開發階段圖表總結：

Duchenne 是一種遺傳性肌肉退化疾病，主要影響男孩，症狀通常在三到五歲之間表現出來。Duchenne 是一種進行性、不可逆且最終致命的疾病，影響約每 5,000 名活產男性中有一人，美國單獨就有估計 10,000 到 15,000 個病例，每年至少有 400 個 Duchenne 新生兒。Duchenne 是由於 dystrophin 基因的變異，導致 dystrophin 蛋白的缺乏或近乎缺乏。Dystrophin 蛋白用以強化肌肉纖維並保護其免受日常磨損。Dystrophin 蛋白同時也是 dystrophin 糖蛋白複合體（"DGC"）的基石，這是一羣連結肌肉細胞內外零組件的蛋白質，以確保肌肉功能正常。在缺乏功能性的 dystrophin 和 DGC 時，肌肉會因日常活動而遭受過度損傷且無法再生，導致纖維化或疤痕組織以及脂肪組織的堆積。已識別出超過 1,000 種 dystrophin 基因變異，這些變異可能是遺傳或自發產生。Duchenne 患者在他們的青少年時期通常會失去行走能力，並依賴輪椅來移動。到他們 20 歲時，患者基本上會從頸部以下癱瘓，並需要呼吸器來呼吸。雖然疾病嚴重程度和預期壽命會有所差異，但患者的生活品質會隨時間顯著下降，通常在早年成年階段因心臟或呼吸系統併發症而死亡。
目前尚無治療 Duchenne 的方法。糖皮質激素治療，現為標準療法，已被證明可以暫時改善肌肉強度、延長行走時間並減緩 Duchenne 的進展。然而，糖皮質激素的使用會伴隨廣為人知的不良副作用，包括：嚴重體重增加、生長受阻、骨結構變弱以及代謝功能異常，等等。最常使用的糖皮質激素包括 prednisone 和 deflazacort（EMFLAZA）。
儘管最近有治療進展，包括美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准的 ELEVIDYS®，一種用於 Duchenne 患者的基因轉移療法，我們認為 Duchenne 代表了一個重要的未滿足醫療需求，同時也是一個社會和經濟負擔。經濟負擔包括醫院入院、藥物、頻繁的醫生訪問以及投資在
輔助裝置的費用，以及間接費用，例如照顧者生產力損失以及因疼痛、焦慮和社會障礙所產生的費用。只有少數 Duchenne 患者會就業，許多照顧者會減少工作時數或完全停止工作，以照顧他們的孩子，這些孩子逐漸需要更多幫助來處理日常任務，例如進食、穿衣和使用廁所。在某些情況下，患者也會經歷嚴重的心理健康問題，需要額外的支持和治療。

我們的領先神經肌肉、研究中的基因轉移候選藥物 SGT-003，是設計用來解決 Duchenne 的根本遺傳原因，透過遞送合成的轉基因，產生 microdystrophin，一種類似 dystrophin 的蛋白質，保留了完整 dystrophin 基因的關鍵零組件，但足夠小以符合 AAV 包裝限制，且主要在身體肌肉中表達，包括骨骼、心臟和呼吸肌肉。AAV-SLB101，用於 SGT-003 的衣殼，是由修改一種自然存在的、非病原性病毒 AAV 所產生，目標是增強其進入骨骼、橫膈膜和心臟肌肉組織的效率。2026 年 3 月，我們開始使用標記 POLARIS-101TM 來代表我們的 AAV-SLB101 衣殼產品（"POLARIS-101TM"）。

我們的 microdystrophin 基於在密蘇裏大學和華盛頓大學以及其他學術機構進行了三十多年的開發和優化工作。在臨牀前研究中，華盛頓大學 Jeffrey Chamberlain 博士和密蘇裏大學 Dongsheng Duan 博士的實驗室，識別出一種專利的遺傳零組件組合，當系統性給予時，會產生功能性 microdystrophin 蛋白表達，不僅穩定肌肉膜並保護肌肉免受傷害，同時也會恢復 DGC 在肌肉膜的定位，顯著增加神經元一氧化氮合酶（"nNOS"）濃度。在已發表的研究中，Duan 博士和 Chamberlain 博士在動物模型中顯示，與較早的組合相比，恢復 nNOS 的 microdystrophin 在改善肌肉功能和抗疲勞方面更有效。

headings: 與我們財務狀況相關的風險及資金需求
自成立以來，我們已產生顯著的淨虧損，並預期在可預見的未來，我們仍將持續產生淨虧損，可能永遠無法實現或維持獲利。
籌措額外資金可能會導致現有股東的股權稀釋，限制我們的營運，或要求我們放棄對我們技術或候選藥物的權利。
我們從未從產品銷售中產生收入，且預期在可預見的未來，若有的話，也不會從產品銷售中產生收入。
我們有限的營運歷史可能使股東難以評估我們業務至今的成功情況，並評估我們未來的生存能力。
不利的全球經濟環境可能損害我們的業務、財務狀況或營運結果。
與我們候選藥物開發相關的風險
我們先前的一項臨牀試驗曾被FDA暫停臨牀試驗，且我們無法保證在未來進行中的、計畫中的及未來的臨牀試驗中不會發生類似事件。
本公司從未完成過臨牀試驗，且可能無法對任何候選藥物（包括SGT-003、SGT-212、SGT-501及其他候選藥物）進行臨牀試驗。
預臨牀研究或早期臨牀試驗的成功結果，可能無法反映後續試驗的結果。
本公司可能在臨牀試驗中遭遇重大延遲，或無法向相關監管機關證明其安全性與有效性。
若本公司第三方臨牀試驗廠商未能遵守嚴格的規範，則本公司任何候選藥物的臨牀試驗可能延遲或失敗。
本公司可能難以招募臨牀試驗參與者，這可能會延遲或阻止本公司進行SGT-003、SGT-212、SGT-501或其他候選藥物的臨牀試驗。
即使本公司完成必要的臨牀試驗，本公司無法預測何時，或是否能獲得監管機構核准商業化候選藥物，且核准可能僅限於較窄的適應症範圍。
即使本公司獲得候選藥物的監管核准，本公司候選藥物仍將受到監管機構的持續監督。
paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列風險因素，除本年度報表 10-K 所包含的其他資訊外，包括本報告中標題為 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析" 的部分，以及我們的財務報表及相關附註。若下列風險因素中所描述的任何事件，或本年度報表 10-K 其他地方所描述的風險發生，將可能嚴重影響我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況，並導致我們普通股的交易價格下跌。本年度報表 10-K 亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。我們的實際結果可能與展望性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，這是因為下列及本年度報表 10-K 其他地方所描述的相關因素所致。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。目前我們尚未知悉的其他風險，或我們認為目前並無重大風險影響我們業務的因素，亦可能影響我們的業務營運。

自成立以來，我們已產生顯著的淨虧損。我們的淨虧損為 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度為 174.3 百萬美元，2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度為 124.7 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 957.8 百萬美元。在 2022 年 12 月收購 AavantiBio, Inc.（"收購"）之前，我們將幾乎所有努力投入於研究與開發，包括 SGT-001 的臨牀開發（我們目前已不再開發），以及 SGT-003 的前期臨牀開發，以及建立我們的管理團隊與基礎設施。收購後，我們將努力投入於其他候選藥物的研發，包括 SGT-003、SGT-212 和 SGT-501 的臨牀開發，以及建立我們的管理團隊。我們預期在數年後纔可能有商業化產品，且我們可能永遠無法有商業化產品。我們預期在可預見的未來將產生顯著費用與營運虧損。我們預期，若我們：
• 在 INSPIRE DUCHENNE、IMPACT DUCHENNE、FALCON 和 ARTEMIS 試驗中納入參與者，並推進 SGT-003、SGT-212 和 SGT-501 的臨牀開發；
• 推進其他候選藥物進入臨牀試驗；
• 繼續進行候選藥物與相關技術（如試劑）的研究與前期臨牀開發；
• 試圖尋找其他候選藥物；• 與美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）及其他監管機關進行監管互動；
